title: WWT Partners Weekly Briefing
description: Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, F5, Intel, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, AWS, Google Cloud and VMware.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 16–27. New: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 26 that Nvidia has told Dell, Supermicro, and other server makers to stop shipping AI servers to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia. The Nov. 17 earnings item was dropped so the Nvidia subsection stayed at four. No new Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, Microsoft, AWS, or Google Cloud announcement dated Nov. 26–27 was opened. F5 and VMware product news were quiet. No new Red Hat press release or Army or Department of War deal dated Nov. 26–27 was found. No new Army or Department of War enterprise agreement was found in Army CIO reporting, ESI, war.gov, Federal News Network, Breaking Defense, DefenseScoop, Nextgov, GovConWire, or vendor newsrooms.

items.headline: Nvidia tells server makers to stop AI shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 26, citing the Financial Times, that Nvidia has ordered manufacturing partners to stop shipping AI servers to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Tom's Hardware said Dell, Supermicro, and other firms that build servers with Nvidia AI GPUs have told customers in those countries that Nvidia has forbidden the shipments. Tom's Hardware said the move follows U.S. rules that closed a loophole letting Chinese AI companies rent compute abroad, and that the rules give cloud providers 90 days to apply for an export license and show their customers are not restricted entities. Tom's Hardware said it is unclear whether Nvidia's order is permanent, and quoted a cloud-provider executive telling the Financial Times that there is a new rule but no guidance on how to apply for the license.

items.headline: Commerce adds Megaspeed and six other firms to the Entity List
items.summary: The Federal Register published Nov. 25 a Bureau of Industry and Security final rule, effective Nov. 23, that adds seven entities in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand to the Entity List. The entities include Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd., plus MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, and Swiftdata. BIS said the End-User Review Committee added them because of the significant risk they will be involved in diverting advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users. The rule requires a license for all items subject to the Export Administration Regulations, says licenses will be reviewed under a presumption of denial, and lets shipments already en route on Nov. 23 proceed if they are completed by Dec. 23.

items.headline: House chairs say Huang will still testify on Nvidia chip smuggling
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 24 that the chairmen of the House Select Committee on China, the House Intelligence Committee, and the House Foreign Affairs Committee said Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter confirmed transcribed interviews on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2. Their statement, quoted by Tom's Hardware, said the board's investigation and Huang's reinstatement do not erase questions about smuggling of Nvidia products, diversion for Chinese military purposes, and China's AI capabilities. Tom's Hardware said Bloomberg reported that Huang will testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, and that Chairman Tim Scott said Huang will testify at a hearing on export controls for advanced AI hardware.

items.headline: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as president and chief executive
items.summary: NVIDIA said Nov. 23 that its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, chief executive, and a board member, effective immediately, after discussions with him and input from senior levels of the U.S. government. The board said that input left it confident the reinstatement poses no national security risk, and that Harvey C. Jones remains chair. NVIDIA said Colette Kress continues as chief financial officer after serving as interim chief executive. The board said an independent-director investigation into reporting that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort will continue, and that NVIDIA is searching for a chief compliance officer.

items.headline: Cisco and Red Hat describe Ansible automation for validated data-center designs
items.summary: Cisco said Nov. 16 that a DevNet discussion with Stephen Fulmer of Red Hat and Archana Sharma of Cisco covered validated designs that ship with Red Hat Ansible automation. Fulmer said the Cisco Intersight Ansible collection has grown to 137 modules and that customers run millions of jobs with it each month. Cisco said that for the Intersight content, Red Hat takes the first support call and triages with Cisco. The post said an AI Pod validated design, using Cisco UCS X-Series and Nexus with Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, and focused on inference, is expected in about a month.

items.headline: AWS Transit Gateway can pass resource context to attached firewalls
items.summary: AWS said Nov. 17 that Transit Gateway can share resource context with attached firewalls, so policies can use VPCs, subnets, security groups, and transit gateway attachments alongside IP addresses. AWS said the gateway embeds that context in the traffic it sends, which lets a firewall apply policy from the first packet without waiting for a tag-to-IP sync. AWS said AWS Network Firewall and Palo Alto Networks software firewalls support the policies. AWS said the feature is available in the commercial regions where Transit Gateway is available, except Bahrain and the UAE, and in AWS GovCloud US-East and US-West.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks says Commerce approved its Secure SI export consortium
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks said Nov. 17 that the U.S. government approved the Secure SI by Design Consortium, which it leads with NVIDIA, IBM, OpenAI, Snowflake, Cognizant, Reflection, Factory, and ServiceNow. The company said the consortium sits under the Commerce Department's American SI Exports Program, part of an SI Action Plan formed in July 2025. Palo Alto Networks said the designation includes government-to-government advocacy, priority export-control licensing reviews, and financing through the Export-Import Bank and the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Intel has started another round of layoffs in its IT organization
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 19, citing Business Insider, that Intel began another round of layoffs in its global IT organization on Nov. 16. Tom's Hardware said Intel has not disclosed how many employees will lose their jobs and has not identified the teams, and that some employees claim the cuts could affect a double-digit share of an IT staff of about 2,607. Tom's Hardware said Intel told Business Insider that it regularly reviews its workforce so people and spending match its priorities. Tom's Hardware said Intel reported 81,100 employees as of Sept. 27, 2026, including subsidiaries, compared with 108,900 a year earlier.

items.headline: Red Hat and Microsoft extend OpenShift virtualization onto Azure's hypervisor
items.summary: Red Hat said Nov. 18 that it is expanding joint engineering with Microsoft so Linux-based and cloud-native platforms on Azure virtual machines can use Microsoft direct virtualization, the same virtualization and hardware access available to Azure-native services. Red Hat said Microsoft Azure Red Hat OpenShift will be one of the first commercial platforms to offer that capability, including Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization as a path off legacy hypervisors. Red Hat said the companies are co-developing support in KubeVirt, Libvirt, QEMU, and the Linux kernel, and that Microsoft is one of the first vendors to extend KubeVirt beyond a KVM hypervisor. Chris Wright, Red Hat's chief technology officer, said the work is meant to let customers modernize virtual machines and run AI workloads on one platform.

items.headline: Red Hat says Azure Red Hat OpenShift IL5 is available on the JWCC contract
items.summary: Red Hat said Nov. 16 that Microsoft Azure Red Hat OpenShift on Microsoft Azure Government, which it said has achieved Impact Level 5 certification, is now available on the Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability contract for Department of War procurement. Red Hat said the certification follows Impact Level 4 in July 2024, and that the service is jointly operated, engineered, and supported by Red Hat and Microsoft, including continuous patching and vulnerability remediation. Red Hat said OpenShift aligns with the DoD Enterprise DevSecOps Reference Design and uses FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 validated cryptography. The post describes availability on an existing contract vehicle, not a new Army enterprise agreement.
